title: Dynamic rollback coordinator with batching/caching cost guardrails
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a centralized rollback coordinator for runtime configuration changes that prioritizes cost-safe decisions for batching and caching recommendations. The coordinator should: (1) evaluate the projected token/unit cost and latency impact of a config change (including batching window, cache TTL and prefix policies, quantization flags) using the Optimize recommendation engine; (2) execute a staged apply (dry-run -> canary -> ramp) with metric-based guardrails; (3) automatically trigger a safe rollback when cost or quality regressions exceed configured thresholds; and (4) reconcile distributed state to ensure no dangling config fragments or KV cache inconsistencies across GPU pools. Goal is to prevent cost regressions caused by aggressive batch/caching changes while enabling safe automated rollouts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Coordinator can receive a proposed config diff and run a deterministic dry-run simulation that returns an estimated delta in per-token cost, per-request latency distribution, and hit-rate for prefix/KV cache.
2) Dry-run estimates within 10% of staging experiment results for common workloads.
3) Canary rollout supports traffic-shaping percentages (1%, 5%, 20%) and automatic promotion/rollback.
4) Rollback triggers: (a) cost increase > 12% sustained over 5 minutes, (b) median latency degradation > 20% against baseline, (c) error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute.
5) Rollbacks are executed as safe reverse-transitions: stop new config acceptance, drain in-flight requests, restore previous runtime kernel/quant flags and cache policies, and run a reconciliation job to repair KV cache entries.
6) Coordinator writes an auditable event for every change and rollback with user, reason, metrics snapshot and links to PR/commit.
7) End-to-end tests and integration tests (including race conditions around cache migration) pass in CI and staging.
8) Behavioral metrics are surfaced in Console: per-change cost delta, rollback count, mean time to rollback, and reconciliation failures.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach:
- Input sources: API change request, PR webhook, Optimize recommendation engine output, and manual changes from Console.
- Pre-apply analysis: run representative request sampler through the simulation harness (use saved prompt buckets) to estimate token amplification and cache hit-rate. Include conservative uncertainty margin.
- Two-phase apply: (A) Dry-run mode applies change only to metric simulator and tagging layer. (B) Canary: apply config to a small set of runtime groups with traffic shaping and short TTLs; collect metrics. (C) Ramp: progressive increase if guardrails pass.
- Guardrail engine: policy DSL that supports metric thresholds, hysteresis windows, and cost-based rules (e.g., only permit batching increase if estimated cost/unit decreases or latency within SLO).
- Reconciliation: idempotent reconciliation loop comparing desired config repo (git-backed) to live runtime state; uses optimistic locking and a per-node transaction to avoid split-brain for KV cache migrations. Provide repair actions and alert on conflicts.
- Rollback mechanism: record inverse change during apply (oplog), provide fast-path restore for runtime flags, and run cache invalidation + gradual warm-up to avoid cold-start latency spikes.
- Telemetry: emit granular events to observability (trace id, metrics snapshot pre/post) and mark config change with change_id.
- Security: sign change bundles, store audit events in encrypted log (KMS).
- Testing: unit harness for guardrail DSL, chaos tests that flip metrics to force rollback, and a staging A/B against production traffic patterns.
- Perf constraints: coordinator decisions must be within 2s for synchronous applies and under 30s for canary orchestration steps.
updates: 2026-02-16: Initial triage meeting with PM and SRE. Agreed P0 due to recent cost incident in batching changes. Assigned Miguel for implementation and Asha for design oversight.

2026-02-25: Spike completed evaluating simulation accuracy using 3 representative workloads. Simulation median error = 8.7% for per-token cost and 9.6% for median latency. Kept conservative margin at +10%.

2026-03-02: Design review held with Runtime, Optimize and Console teams. Key feedback: include a dry-run API endpoint and an 'acceptance window' parameter for hysteresis. Action items created linking to design doc.

2026-03-05: Implemented coordinator core + guardrail DSL prototype. Found race where concurrent canaries could overwrite KV cache migrations; added per-change mutex scoped to runtime-pool. See linked PR.

2026-03-09: Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 — core coordinator and dry-run API. CI green on unit tests; integration tests failing intermittently on reconciliation timing (flaky).

2026-03-12: Fixed reconciliation flakiness by switching to leader-based epoch stamping for reconciliation loop. Canary deployment to staging at 1% traffic initiated. Observed slight initial hit-rate drop (~3%) but no cost regression. Proceeding to 5% canary next week.
2026-03-12: Security review kickoff scheduled; encryption and audit log flow documented in Confluence.
